primarySection.hubTitle: StataNow 19.5 BE Consensus Synthesis & Forest Plots Hub
primarySection.hubText: Locked Protocol Synthesis Standard: TEAS and EA were evaluated separately for primary modality-specific inference (TEAS vs Sham: MD = −14.00 mg, p = 0.1145; EA vs Usual Care: MD = −3.94 mg, p = 0.397). A combined strict-evidence synthesis pooling both modalities (MD = −9.91 mg [−20.08, +0.27], p = 0.0545, k = 7, N = 676) is shown as a supporting contextual analysis. Between-study variance is estimated using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) with Knapp–Hartung confidence intervals and 95% prediction intervals [−39.35, +19.54].

primarySection.trajectoryDisclaimer: Different sets of trials contribute to each cumulative time window. These estimates should therefore not be interpreted as repeated longitudinal measurements of the same study population or as a continuous trajectory of treatment effect.
primarySection.teasStratum: Primary Stratum 1: TEAS vs Sham (k=4, N=337)
primarySection.eaStratum: Primary Stratum 2: EA vs Usual Care (k=3, N=339)
primarySection.threshold10mgNotice: Primary prespecified clinical-importance benchmark: 10 mg IV MME. The pooled average (−9.91 mg, 95% KH CI [−20.08, +0.27]) does not reach that benchmark as a point estimate, and does not reach statistical significance, though individual high-demand surgical cohorts achieve substantial sparing.

metaregStudio.title: StataNow 19.5 BE Meta-Regression & Moderator Studio
metaregStudio.subtitle: Knapp–Hartung random-effects subgroup analysis across the 7 strict primary trials. One univariable meta-regression (modality) is reported and is underpowered; no multivariable model is fitted.
metaregStudio.ruleOf10Text: With k = 7 strict primary trials the analysis does not meet the Cochrane 10:1 minimum study-count rule of thumb (§10.11.4), even for a single predictor. Only one univariable meta-regression (modality) is reported, and it is exploratory and underpowered. No multivariable model is fitted, and Egger-type small-study-effect testing is not performed because k < 10.
metaregStudio.tableTitle: Comprehensive Moderator & Clinical Parameter Matrix (k = 7 Strict Primary RCTs)
metaregStudio.cardEcologicalText: Meta-regression uses study-level averages or proportions. A relationship observed between studies does not necessarily represent the relationship between individual patients within those studies (Simpson's paradox). Evaluating individual patient age, BMI, or sex effects requires Individual Participant Data (IPD) meta-analysis.
metaregStudio.cardStrictaText: In accordance with STRICTA guidelines, acupoints in perioperative anesthesia trials are delivered as standard multi-point somatic prescriptions (e.g. LI4, PC6, ST36, SP6). Because trials administer combinations, statistical collinearity prevents isolating the independent contribution of any single acupoint in study-level meta-regression.

forestPlotHelper.title: How to Read this Forest Plot
forestPlotHelper.item1: The estimated treatment effect for each study. Marker area reflects its statistical weight in the random-effects meta-analysis.
forestPlotHelper.item2: 95% confidence interval for each study estimate, reflecting statistical precision.
forestPlotHelper.item3: The pooled random-effects average. Diamond width spans the 95% confidence interval.
forestPlotHelper.item4: Vertical dashed line (0 for MD/SMD; 1.0 for RR). Values to the left favor TEAS/EA.
forestPlotHelper.item5: Extended dashed bracket estimating the plausible true effect in a future comparable clinical setting.

gradeHelper.high: High Certainty: Very confident that the true effect lies close to the estimate.
gradeHelper.moderate: Moderate Certainty: Moderately confident in effect estimate; true effect likely close, but could differ.
gradeHelper.low: Low Certainty: Confidence in effect estimate is limited; true effect may be substantially different.
gradeHelper.veryLow: Very Low Certainty: Very little confidence in effect estimate; true effect likely substantially different.
gradeHelper.rob: Risk of Bias: Assesses potential methodological bias affecting contributing trials.
gradeHelper.inconsistency: Inconsistency: Assesses unexplained heterogeneity and variance across study results.
gradeHelper.indirectness: Indirectness: Assesses differences in populations, interventions, or outcomes relative to review question.
gradeHelper.imprecision: Imprecision: Assesses uncertainty and width of confidence intervals relative to clinical decision thresholds.
gradeHelper.pubBias: Publication Bias: Assesses potential selective publication of positive or statistically significant findings.

interpretations.primary24h: Across the 7 strict primary trials (N = 676), the combined synthesis of perioperative electrical acupoint stimulation showed an estimated 24-hour postoperative opioid reduction of 9.91 mg IV morphine equivalents (95% KH CI [−20.08, +0.27] mg, p = 0.0545, tau2 = 113.91, I2 = 98.57%; 95% PI [−39.35, +19.54]). Modality-specific analyses: TEAS vs sham (k = 4, N = 337) showed MD = −14.00 mg (95% KH CI [−34.18, +6.19], p = 0.1145), and EA vs control (k = 3, N = 339) showed MD = −3.94 mg (95% KH CI [−19.77, +11.90], p = 0.397). Because the Knapp–Hartung confidence intervals include zero across all strata, evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant 24-hour opioid-sparing effect.
interpretations.teasStratum: In the double-blind sham-controlled TEAS stratum (k = 4 strict trials: Chen 1998, Chen 2020, He 2026, Szmit 2021; N = 337), opioid sparing averaged 14.00 mg IV MME (Knapp–Hartung 95% CI [−34.18, +6.19], p = 0.1145, tau2 = 156.88, I2 = 98.59%). High between-study heterogeneity reflects differing surgical baseline pain and anesthesia protocols.
interpretations.eaStratum: In the needle electroacupuncture stratum (k = 3 strict trials: El-Rakshy 2009, Seevaunnamtum 2016, Yang 2024; N = 339), opioid sparing averaged 3.94 mg IV MME (Knapp–Hartung 95% CI [−19.77, +11.90], p = 0.397, tau2 = 28.47, I2 = 77.15%). Across all 6 leave-one-out sensitivity models, omission of any single trial leaves the 95% confidence interval spanning zero.
interpretations.opioid48h: At 48 hours postoperatively (Target A strict: k = 3 trials, N = 1,999), cumulative opioid reduction averaged 10.27 mg IV MME (95% KH CI [−34.83, +14.30], p = 0.2139; REML + Knapp–Hartung, tau2 = 94.56, I2 = 97.07%). Excluding An 2014 yields MD = −12.40 mg (p = 0.405), while broader inclusion of Xie 2014 yields MD = −12.30 mg (p = 0.073).
interpretations.modalityMultivar: The apparent raw difference between EA and TEAS (unadjusted difference −9.32 mg, p = 0.308) was not statistically significant. Meta-regression between modalities is underpowered (k = 7 < 10) and demonstrates no statistically detectable difference in opioid sparing between transcutaneous electrodes and needle electroacupuncture.
interpretations.primaryOpioid: Across the 7 strict primary trials (N = 676), the combined synthesis of perioperative electrical acupoint stimulation showed an estimated 24-hour postoperative opioid reduction of 9.91 mg IV morphine equivalents (95% KH CI [−20.08, +0.27] mg, p = 0.0545, tau2 = 113.91, I2 = 98.57%; 95% PI [−39.35, +19.54]). Modality-specific analyses: TEAS vs sham (k = 4, N = 337) showed MD = −14.00 mg (95% KH CI [−34.18, +6.19], p = 0.1145), and EA vs control (k = 3, N = 339) showed MD = −3.94 mg (95% KH CI [−19.77, +11.90], p = 0.397). tooltip.reml: Restricted Maximum Likelihood: Estimator used in primary random-effects meta-analysis to estimate between-study variance (τ²).
tooltip.knappHartung: Knapp–Hartung adjustment: Provides robust standard errors and confidence intervals in random-effects meta-analysis, especially with limited study counts.
tooltip.i2: I² statistic: Percentage of variability in effect estimates due to between-study heterogeneity rather than sampling chance.
tooltip.metaRegressionR2: Meta-regression R²: Proportion of between-study variance accounted for by the moderator; not individual patient variance.
